title: Whole House Dehumidifier Installation: Steps, Options & Cost
h1: Whole-House Dehumidifier Installation: What to Expect
dek: Ducting layouts, drains, wiring, controls and what it really costs — a clear walkthrough before you call an HVAC contractor.
description: Whole house dehumidifier installation explained: ducting layouts, condensate drains, electrical and controls, typical installed costs, and DIY vs. pro.
intro: A whole-house dehumidifier is a bigger commitment than a portable unit, but it's the most hands-off way to control humidity: no buckets, no machines in your living space, just steady, dry air delivered through your ductwork. A good **whole house dehumidifier installation** depends on choosing the right ducting layout, planning a reliable condensate drain, and wiring and controlling it correctly.

Most homeowners hire an HVAC contractor for this, and for good reason — the work touches ductwork, electrical and drainage. But knowing how it's done helps you compare quotes, ask the right questions and avoid an install that underperforms.
Here's how whole-home dehumidifiers connect, what the installation involves, what it typically costs and when a DIY install is realistic.

products.name: Aprilaire E100 Whole-House Dehumidifier
cons: Large unit needs a mechanical space
products.whyWeLoveIt: The E100 is one of the most widely installed whole-home dehumidifiers, flexible enough to tie into existing HVAC ducts or run with its own, and efficient enough to justify running all season.
products.performance: Aprilaire rates it at up to 100 pints a day and coverage up to about 5,500 square feet. Contractors are familiar with it, which makes quotes and service easier to find. See more in our [best whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Honeywell DR90A3000 Whole-House Dehumidifier
pros: Designed to integrate with HVAC ductwork
cons: Less suited to homes without ducts
products.whyWeLoveIt: If your home already has forced-air heating and cooling, the DR90A3000 is built to slot into that system, delivering dry air to every room through the vents you already have.
products.performance: It's rated at 90 pints per day and is typically installed beside the furnace or air handler with its own dehumidistat control. Like any ducted unit, it needs a properly trapped condensate drain. Compare it with others in our [best Honeywell dehumidifier](/best/best-honeywell-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Santa Fe Ultra V100 Ventilating Dehumidifier
pros: Brings in filtered fresh air while drying
cons: Extra fresh-air duct adds install complexity
products.whyWeLoveIt: Tight, energy-efficient homes often need fresh air as well as dry air. The Ultra V100 handles both, pulling in outdoor air through a dedicated duct, filtering it and drying it before it's distributed.
products.performance: Santa Fe rates it at 100 pints a day for homes up to about 2,300 square feet, with MERV-13 filtration and an 8-inch fresh-air duct connection. It's a strong choice for newer homes that run stuffy and humid. More in our [best Santa Fe dehumidifier](/best/best-santa-fe-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: Your contractor will choose a layout based on your duct system, where the unit can go and whether your home also needs ventilation. Ask them to explain why they chose the layout they recommend.

sections.heading: How to install a whole house dehumidifier: the steps

items: **Size the unit.** The contractor estimates the moisture load from square footage, climate, airtightness and occupancy.
**Choose the location.** Usually a basement, utility room, crawl space or attic near the air handler, with access for filter changes.
**Mount the unit.** Set it on a platform or suspend it as the manual allows. Attic installs typically need a secondary drain pan.
**Connect the ducts.** Cut in the intake and supply connections, add a backdraft damper where needed and seal all joints.
**Run the condensate drain.** Install a trapped drain line to a floor drain, sump or condensate pump.
**Wire power and controls.** Connect to a dedicated outlet or circuit, and install the dehumidistat or wall control.
**Commission and test.** Verify airflow, drainage and that humidity falls to the set point, usually around 45–50%.
**Gravity drain** to a floor drain or sump pit — simplest and most reliable.
**Condensate pump** when no downhill route exists — choose one with a safety switch.
**Shared HVAC drain** — possible in some setups, but confirm it can handle the volume.

blocks.text: A whole-house unit can produce gallons of water a day in humid weather, so the drain must be reliable. In attics or above finished spaces, overflow protection is essential.

Most residential whole-house dehumidifiers use a standard 115-volt supply, ideally on a dedicated circuit. Controls vary: some units come with a wall-mounted dehumidistat, while others integrate with compatible smart thermostats. If the unit should run with the HVAC blower, the installer will wire the control so the fan comes on when the dehumidifier calls.

sections.heading: How much does whole house dehumidifier installation cost?

head: Item
Typical estimate
blocks.caption: Typical estimates only. Costs vary by region, home size, duct layout and access.

blocks.text: Running costs matter too. A whole-home unit can run for hundreds of hours each summer, so ENERGY STAR Most Efficient models pay back over time. See our [dehumidifier electricity guide](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/).

A freestanding whole-house unit with simple ducting is within reach for an experienced DIYer. But tying into HVAC ducts, wiring controls to the air handler and planning drainage are jobs most homeowners leave to a licensed HVAC contractor. Some manufacturers require professional installation for full warranty coverage, so read the terms first, and check whether your area requires a permit.

blocks.title: Questions to ask your installer
blocks.text: Which layout will you use and why? Where will the condensate drain? Is a backdraft damper included? Who handles electrical work and permits? What does the labor warranty cover?

A well-planned whole house dehumidifier installation gives you invisible, automatic humidity control. Choose a layout that fits your ducts, insist on a reliable condensate drain and plan for dedicated power and a good control. Expect roughly $2,000–$4,500 installed for most homes. The **Aprilaire E100** is our all-around pick, the **Honeywell DR90A3000** suits forced-air systems and the **Santa Fe Ultra V100** adds fresh-air ventilation. If you only need to dry a crawl space, see our [crawl space dehumidifier installation](/guides/crawl-space-dehumidifier-installation/) guide, or compare installed and freestanding options in [best wall-mounted dehumidifiers](/best/best-wall-mounted-dehumidifier/).

faqs.q: How much does a whole house dehumidifier cost installed?
faqs.a: As a typical estimate, most homeowners pay about $2,000–$4,500 for a whole-house dehumidifier installed. Complex jobs involving attic installs, new ductwork or ventilation can exceed $5,000.

faqs.q: How is a whole house dehumidifier installed?
faqs.a: The unit is sized, placed near the air handler or in a utility space, connected to ductwork, given a trapped condensate drain, wired to power and a control, then commissioned to confirm airflow and drainage.

faqs.q: Can I install a whole house dehumidifier myself?
faqs.a: Experienced DIYers can install a freestanding unit with simple ducting. HVAC integration, electrical work and drainage are usually best left to a licensed contractor, and some warranties require professional installation.

faqs.q: Where should a whole house dehumidifier be installed?
faqs.a: Typically in a basement, utility room, crawl space or attic near the HVAC air handler, with access for maintenance and a nearby drain.

faqs.q: Is a whole home dehumidifier worth the cost?
faqs.a: In humid climates, tightly built homes or houses where AC leaves the air clammy, often yes. It delivers consistent humidity control throughout the home without buckets or portable units.

faqs.q: Does a whole house dehumidifier need its own circuit?
faqs.a: A dedicated circuit is recommended because the unit can run for long periods. Your installer or electrician will confirm what your unit requires.
